title: Managed app-server daemon keeps every old release, ~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases grew to 2.8 GB

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.161.0 (brew cask). The managed app-server daemon is also 0.161.0.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6.1-sol, but i dont think the model is related.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

iTerm2 3.7.3

### What issue are you seeing?

The managed daemon updater installs every new release into `~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases/<version>-aarch64-apple-darwin/`, but it never removes the old ones. Only `current` is used.

On my Mac there were 9 release folders after 13 days:

```
0.157.0  314M  Sep 25
0.157.1  314M  Sep 26
0.158.0  316M  Sep 28
0.159.0  316M  Sep 29
0.159.2  316M  Sep 30
0.159.3  316M  Oct 1
0.160.0  318M  Oct 2
0.160.1  318M  Oct 7
0.161.0  321M  Oct 7   (current)
```

Total was 2.8 GB. With a new release almost every day this is around 200 MB per day and it never stops.

i looked at `codex-rs/app-server-daemon` (`lib.rs`, `managed_install.rs`, `migration.rs`) and `scripts/install/install.sh` on main and i couldnt find any code that removes previous release folders. Maybe i missed it.

The CLI here is installed with brew, so these copies grow quietly next to the brew install and most users will not notice them.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install Codex CLI (brew cask in my case) and use it normally, so the managed daemon starts. No `~/.codex/app-server-daemon/settings.json`, so auto update is on.
2. Wait for a few daemon auto updates. It checks 5 minutes after start and then every hour.
3. Run:

```sh
ls ~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases
du -sh ~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases
```

### What is the expected behavior?

After a successful update and restart, old releases are removed. Keeping `current` and maybe one previous release for rollback would be enough.

If keeping them is on purpose, a retention setting or a cleanup command under `codex app-server daemon`, and a short note in the README, would help.

### Additional information

- i deleted the 7 old folders by hand and kept 0.161.0 (current) and 0.160.1. The daemon kept running, and `codex app-server daemon version` reports `cliVersion`, `appServerVersion` and `managedCodexVersion` all as 0.161.0. So manual cleanup looks safe, but users should not need to do it.
- Related but different: #48195 (each release is a full package copy, about 374 MB) and #51961 (daemon and updater start without explicit settings).
